subject: Harvest.ai: LlamaIndex tracing + Redwood SDK sandbox plan
messages:
From: Tom Liu <tom@harvest.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Harvest POC: LlamaIndex trace capture into Redwood

Hi Soojin + Vanessa,

Appreciate you taking this — I'm Tom from Harvest's integrations team. We're evaluating runtime telemetry for chains constructed with LlamaIndex and want to capture prompts, step-level timing, and token counts into Redwood's tracing layer so our analytics dashboards can stitch executions to user sessions.

High-level ask: can Redwood stand up a short sandbox (2-week POC) where we exercise a few representative LlamaIndex pipelines and validate trace fidelity + attribution? Our product folks included a short spec (attached) with three pipelines: retrieval-augmented QA, multi-turn summarization with intermediate steps, and an embed+search rerank.

Constraints:
- We need to preserve prompt text for drift analysis but can mask PII at ingestion.
- We'll run from our staging k8s cluster (public egress) and can install a lightweight SDK sidecar.
- Prefer to use existing LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters if you already support them.

Can we do a kickoff early next week? If so, please share a brief onboarding checklist and any pre-auth tokens we should request.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Liu
Integrations Lead, Harvest Analytics
Attachments: harvest_poc_spec.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Liu <tom@harvest.ai>, soojin_lee@redwood.ai

Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Harvest POC: LlamaIndex trace capture into Redwood

Tom — quick technical notes ahead of the kickoff so we can scope the adapter work:

Thanks for the spec. A few clarifying Qs:

- Are you currently using LlamaIndex's default callback system, or a custom runner? If default, we can wire into the existing callback hooks (LM events, retriever events, node outputs). If custom, we'll need the repo or a small reproducible example.

- For KV cache snapshotting: do you want KV cache presence captured as a boolean per-span, or do you plan to persist snapshots to object storage and reference them by id? We recommend boolean + snapshot id to save on trace size.

- Prompt hashing: we typically compute a salted hash (sha256 with tenant salt) and send that as span.attributes.prompt_hash so you can join without storing raw prompt text. If you need raw text for QA, we can make that an opt-in field for PII-scrubbed payloads.

- Instrumentation format: we prefer an OpenTelemetry-compatible span with attributes: model.name, model.variant, prompt_hash, token_count_input, token_count_output, step.name. Example span pseudocode (curl):

  curl -X POST https://ingest.redwood.ai/v1/spans -H 'Authorization: Bearer <INGEST_KEY>' -d '{"trace": {"spans": [{"attributes": {"model.name":"gpt-jr","prompt_hash":"<hash>","token_count_input":23}}]}}'

If you're planning to reuse LangChain adapters, note the minor difference in event naming between LangChain->LlamaIndex wrappers; we'll include a small shim in the onboarding repo. Attaching a lightweight example (trace_handshake_example.json) that shows expected attributes.

If you can confirm the callback style and whether snapshots are needed, we'll finalize the tech plan at kickoff.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Software Engineer, Instrumentation
Redwood Inference
Attachments: trace_handshake_example.json (application/json)
